items.title: Two Kinds of Undistorted Recognition: Knowing a Genuine Decline for What It Is

items.zh: 謂如有一，得初靜慮，便生喜足，不求上進，唯起愛味。由起如是欲俱行想作意故，遂便退失近欲界定。彼於此衰能了是衰，由此因緣，當知無倒。又由所得靜慮定故，自譽毀他。謂我所得此靜慮定，非餘能得。由起如此欲俱行想作意故，所有蓋纏轉增轉厚，便從定退。彼於此衰能了是衰，又以所得靜慮諸定顯示於他，為諸國王及王臣等當供養我。從定起已，尋思此事。由如是欲俱行想作意故，所有蓋纏轉增轉厚，餘如前說。如是當知修靜慮者於三摩地退失無倒。第二無倒，翻初無倒，應知其相。此二無倒，亦於二時應知其相。由依如是倒無倒處，安立四轉。
items.en: Someone who, having attained the first dhyāna, at once feels satisfied and seeks no further advancement, giving rise only to relish — through this craving-accompanied attention arising again and again, he falls away from the concentration that borders the desire realm, the first dhyāna itself. Recognising this decline as decline, he is, for this reason, undistorted. Again, on account of the dhyāna attained, one praises oneself and disparages others, thinking "this dhyāna I have attained, others cannot attain" — through this craving-accompanied attention, the hindrances and their entanglements thicken and grow, and one falls from the concentration. Recognising this decline as decline, one is likewise undistorted. The second undistorted case is the reverse of the first, and its character should be understood accordingly. Both undistorted cases, too, should be understood as occurring at their own proper occasions. By these instances of distortion and non-distortion, the four permutations are established.

items.title: The Four-Fold Check: Inferior, Superior, Excellent, and Supreme Concentration

items.zh: 復次，如分別四撿行定經中，由四種相，撿行一切三摩地等。謂此等持是順退分，乃至此是順決擇分。云何撿行？謂此是劣分、此是勝分、此殊勝分、此最勝分、如其次第。
items.en: Furthermore, as the Sūtra Distinguishing the Four Ways of Checking Concentration says: by four marks, one checks all unifications and the rest — whether this concentration is retrogression-prone, and so on up to whether it is penetration-prone [towards the uncontaminated]. What is "checking"? That this is the inferior grade, this the superior grade, this the excellent grade, this the supreme grade, in that order.

items.zh: 謂修定者，從初靜慮還退出已，於諸靜慮不復樂入，亦不思惟此行狀相。然欲俱行諸想作意數數現前，如先所說，從彼起已隨念愛味。當於爾時，修靜慮者應自撿行：我三摩地今成退劣。又修定者，從初靜慮還退出已，得聞隨順此定教法。謂初靜慮諸行狀相。慇懃懇到善取其相，令所得定堅住不忘。如是隨念順定法故，成順住分。當於爾時，應自撿行：我三摩地已成其勝，我三摩地已得安住，非退、非進、非趣決擇。
items.en: A meditator who, having fallen back from the first dhyāna, no longer delights in entering any of the dhyānas, nor attends to their practice, state, and mark — while craving-accompanied thoughts arise again and again, and, as said before, relish follows upon emerging — such a one, at that time, should check himself: "my concentration has now become inferior and retrogression-prone." Again, a meditator who, having fallen back from the first dhyāna, hears the teaching that accords with that concentration — the first dhyāna's practice, state, and mark — and earnestly, thoroughly grasps it well, so that the concentration attained stands firm and is not forgotten, thereby recollecting the teaching that accords with concentration, becomes stability-prone. At that time, he should check himself: "my concentration has now become superior; my concentration now abides — neither retrogressing, nor advancing, nor heading towards penetration."

items.title: Excellent and Supreme Concentration: Advancing to the Second Dhyāna, and Opening onto Uncontaminated Insight

items.zh: 又靜慮者，從初靜慮還退出已，得聞隨順第二靜慮教授之法；既得聞已，第二靜慮道俱行諸想作意數數現前。當於爾時，應自撿行：我三摩地已成殊勝，非退、非住，唯是勝進，非趣決擇。
items.en: Again, a meditator who, having fallen back from the first dhyāna, hears the teaching that accords with the second dhyāna, and, having heard it, gives rise again and again to the thoughts and attention that accompany the path of the second dhyāna, should at that time check himself: "my concentration has now become excellent — neither retrogressing nor merely abiding, but genuinely advancing, though not yet heading towards penetration."

items.zh: 又修定者，從初靜慮還退出已，聞苦諦等相相應教法；既得聞已，苦諦等俱行諸想作意順決擇分數數現前。彼於爾時，當自撿行：我三摩地已成最勝，非退、非住，亦非勝進，然趣決擇。
items.en: Again, a meditator who, having fallen back from the first dhyāna, hears the teaching corresponding to the mark of the truth of suffering and the rest, and, having heard it, gives rise again and again to the thoughts and attention that accompany the truth of suffering and the rest, conducing to penetration, should at that time check himself: "my concentration has now become supreme — neither retrogressing, nor merely abiding, nor simply advancing, but heading towards penetration."

items.title: Not Taking Up Any Perception: How a Practitioner in Deep Concentration Relates to the Six Sense-Fields

items.zh: 復次，如經言：有眼、有色、乃至有意、有法；而諸苾芻，於此諸法若實若有都不領受。尚不受想，何況無想。此復云何？謂諸苾芻於初靜慮具足安住，由此因緣，厭壞眼色乃至意法。由厭壞故威勢映奪，遂於眼中無有眼想，然有其想；乃至於法無有法想，然有其想。云何有想？謂於眼等，作意思惟是苦、是集，或是病等，彼於諸法不受自相。如是乃至無所有處。此中正說無漏作意。
items.en: Furthermore, as the sūtra says: "there is the eye, there is form" — and so on up through "there is mind, there is a mind-object" — yet monks do not take these dharmas as real or as existent; they do not even take up perception of them, still less what is free of all perception of marks. Monks who abide fully in the first dhyāna, by this very cause, weary of and break down [attachment to] the eye and form, up through mind and mind-objects. Through this wearying-and-breaking-down, its force overwhelms and displaces [the ordinary perception], so that in the eye there is no [ordinary] perception of an eye — yet there is still a perception; and so on up to: in a mind-object there is no [ordinary] perception of a mind-object — yet there is still a perception. What is this perception? Attending to the eye and the rest, contemplating them as suffering, as origin, or as disease, one does not take up the self-mark of these dharmas. So it continues up through the sphere of nothingness. This refers specifically to uncontaminated attention.

items.zh: 云何名為不受無想？謂不思惟一切相故，於盡滅中思惟寂靜。此中意說離諸相想，名為無想。又說安住滅盡定者，一切諸想皆不生起。

items.title: Four Ways to Approach the Path: Calm-First, Insight-First, and Their Pairings With Dhyāna and Insight

items.zh: 復次，如經中說四種趣道。云何宴坐，於諸法中思惟簡擇？謂有苾芻，先已證得初靜慮等，而未見諦。由聽正法及多聞故，而能宴坐，依三摩地，於苦等諦發起現觀。如是行者，依增上心，修增上慧。
items.en: Furthermore, as the sūtra speaks of four ways of approaching the path. What is it to sit in stillness, contemplating and discerning among all phenomena? There is a monk who has already attained the first dhyāna and the rest, but has not yet seen the truths. Through hearing the true teaching and through extensive learning, he is able to sit in stillness and, resting on his concentration, gives rise to direct realisation of the truth of suffering and the rest. Such a practitioner cultivates heightened wisdom by resting on heightened mind.

items.title: The Second Way: Heightened Wisdom Giving Rise to Heightened Mind

items.zh: 又有苾芻，如實知苦乃至知道，而未證得初靜慮等。彼便宴坐，思惟諸法。如是行者，依增上慧，修增上心。
items.en: Again, there is a monk who truly knows suffering, up through truly knowing the path, yet has not attained even the first dhyāna. He then sits in stillness, contemplating the Dharma. Such a practitioner cultivates heightened mind by resting on heightened wisdom.

blocks.text: Today's reading teaches a meditator to evaluate his own practice honestly: to recognise genuine decline, to check which grade of concentration he has, and to see which of four ways of approaching the path he is following.

subs.head: Knowing decline for what it is

blocks.text: Yesterday's distortion has an opposite: undistorted recognition. Relishing the first dhyāna, one "falls back from the concentration near the desire realm". Venerable Miào Jìng: that is the first dhyāna itself, "adjacent to the desire realm"; one loses it through relish. Master Cháng Bǎi adopts Venerable Miào Jìng's reading of the two undistorted cases: one knows a decline caused by relish, self-exaltation, and greed; and one knows the absence of decline when there is no relish, exaltation, or clinging.

A practitioner checks his concentration as **inferior**, **superior**, **excellent**, or **supreme**. The inferior falls back; the superior stays; the excellent advances to the next dhyāna; the supreme, on hearing teachings on the truths, gives rise to thoughts that accompany the truths and lead towards penetration. The highest grade of concentration is defined not by depth but by its opening onto insight.

A sūtra says monks in deep concentration "do not take up" perceptions of earth, water, this world, or the next, as real. Venerable Miào Jìng: "When sunlight appears, moonlight no longer shows; when the wisdom of mindfulness appears, the old discrimination of self and mine vanishes." The perceptions are not suppressed by force; they lose their hold in the light of insight. And "still less a total absence of perception": Venerable Miào Jìng: not the no-perception attainment, but not thinking of any sign, signlessness.

subs.head: Four ways to approach the path

blocks.text: Four ways a practitioner reaches the path:

items: **Calm first**: "a monk who has already attained the first dhyāna and the rest, but has not yet seen the truths", who then, through hearing the teaching and resting on concentration, discerns phenomena.
**Insight first**: one who truly knows the truths but lacks the first dhyāna. Venerable Miào Jìng: he practised the foundations of mindfulness in threshold concentration and attained stream-entry.

blocks.text: The treatise sums up: the first draws forth the path of seeing; the second and third, the path of cultivation; the fourth, both. There is no single correct order: some begin with deep concentration, some with insight, and the path accommodates both, so long as both are eventually present. This is reassuring for practitioners who find deep absorption difficult.

quiz.q: Relishing the first dhyāna, one "falls back from the concentration near the desire realm." How does Venerable Miào Jìng read this?
options: it is the first dhyāna itself, adjacent to the desire realm — one loses the first dhyāna
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'Concentration near the desire realm' is the first dhyāna — adjacent to the desire realm — and it is lost." Knowing one's error is "undistorted." The translation's "falls back to a state near the desire realm" differs (logged).

quiz.q: Whose reading of the two undistorted cases does Master Cháng Bǎi ultimately adopt?
options: Venerable Miào Jìng — decline from relish, self-exaltation, and greed is the first; not relishing, exalting, or coveting when flourishing, and so not declining, is the second
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Venerable holds the first undistorted case is knowing one's decline caused by relish, self-exaltation, and greed"; "when concentration flourishes, without relish, exaltation, or greed, it doesn't decline." He states this reading is more reasonable. The note's "doesn't settle it" is wrong.

quiz.q: In the fourfold check, what is the supreme grade?
options: hearing teachings on the truths, thoughts accompanying the truths arise repeatedly towards penetration — not declining, abiding, or merely advancing, but heading towards penetration
quiz.why: "Hears the teaching corresponding to the mark of the truth of suffering and the rest … should at that time check himself: 'my concentration has now become supreme — neither retrogressing, nor merely abiding, nor simply advancing, but heading towards penetration.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: the dhyānas alone leave one ordinary.

quiz.q: The sūtra says monks don't take dharmas as real or existent. What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use for "its force overwhelms and displaces"?
options: when the sun rises the moon fades — when mindfulness-wisdom appears, the old self-and-mine discrimination vanishes
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When sunlight appears, moonlight no longer shows; when the wisdom of mindfulness appears, the old discrimination of self and mine" disappears. Master Cháng Bǎi: this follows the *Saṃyukta*, Miào Jìng, and Kuiji, not the *Pixunji*.

quiz.q: In "still less a total absence of perception," what does Venerable Miào Jìng say "absence of perception" means?
options: not thinking of any sign — signlessness, not the no-perception attainment
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Not thinking of any sign — that's 'no perception'; not the no-perception of that attainment." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing Kuiji: in cessation no perceptions arise, neither taking up perception nor its absence. The translation's "total absence of perception" differs (logged).

quiz.q: What kind of practitioner is the first way — sitting in stillness discerning phenomena?
options: having attained the first dhyāna but not seen the truths, through hearing and learning, resting on concentration, he realises the truths — cultivating wisdom on the basis of mind
quiz.why: "A monk who has already attained the first dhyāna and the rest, but has not yet seen the truths. Through hearing the true teaching and extensive learning … resting on his concentration, gives rise to direct realisation … cultivates heightened wisdom by resting on heightened mind." Venerable Miào Jìng: "mind" here is concentration.

quiz.q: The second way: truly knowing the truths but without the first dhyāna. On what basis, per Venerable Miào Jìng, did this person attain stream-entry?
options: threshold concentration — practising the four foundations in it and attaining stream-entry
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This person attained threshold concentration and, practising the four foundations of mindfulness in it, reached stream-entry." Only a stream-enterer truly knows suffering; with dhyāna comes the third fruit, then arhatship.
